title: Dovetail weekly kernel + KV scrub
summary: This doc collects the weekly standup scrub focused on kernel cooperativity changes, KV cache shadowing experiments, and batching heuristics adjustments. Goal: synthesize outcomes from experiments, call out action items for the next sprint, and capture transient notes from the Friday architecture sync.
highlights: Ran three kernel cooperativity variants (quantum=2/4/8) against microbatch path
KV shadow-warmup reduced first-token p99 for long-chat flows by ~18% in lab traces
New coalescer backoff patch (PR 9876) decreased jitter under bursty traffic but increased tail under synthetic uniform loads
experiments: kv-shadow-warmup: ran across canary fleet (n=16 gpus) using 30m traffic replay, result: median latency down 12ms, 95p down 29ms
kernel-quantum-4: stable with sequence lengths <=512, observed throughput drop on long sequences (>1k) — hypothesis: kernel handshake cost increased
coalescer-backoff-alpha: toggled alpha from 0.3->0.6; reduced microburst stalls but increased average batch size by ~7%
metrics_snapshot: Canary cluster (c-canary-03) baseline: 95p infer latency 148ms. After kv-shadow: 95p = 121ms. Throughput per-GPU (tokens/s) baseline 78k, after kernel-quantum-4 74k on short seqs, 63k on long seqs.
action_items: Samir: open follow-up with runtime-kernel team to profile handshake overhead at sequence lengths >1024 (due 2029-07-19)
Liu: run kv-shadow experiment with higher prefix cache hit ratio (target 40%) and report dataset variance (due 2029-07-18)
Mariana: rollback coalescer alpha change for prod canary and schedule A/B with traffic shaping (due 2029-07-20)
Priya: draft concise oncall checklist for kernel fallback sequence (due 2029-07-17)
blockers: Memory accounting bug in thinstate bridge causing occasional double-eviction under high concurrency (ticket JIRA-ENG-7142)
Limited canary capacity for long-sequence replication — need additional reserved GPUs from infra team
next_steps: Experiment matrix for kernel quantum x prefill strategy to be scheduled next week
Instrument per-request KV warmup latency with trace id to correlate requests to cache hits
Add regression test to CI that simulates bursty arrival patterns and verifies coalescer fallbacks
retrospective_notes: We are converging on a middle-ground quantum (4) for most workloads but need a dynamic switch for heavy long-sequence flows. KV shadow warmup shows promise but is sensitive to prefix hit distribution. The coalescer tuning revealed that single-parameter knobs (alpha) move multiple metrics; next iteration should target multi-dimensional policies (alpha + max_hold_ms).
